title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: The playing court shall be measured 94 feet in length by 50 feet in width. The three-point field goal line is 23 feet 9 inches from the center of the basket, 22 feet in the corners. The free throw line is 15 feet from the backboard.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: Each team shall consist of five players on the court. No team may be reduced to fewer than five players; if a player receives his sixth personal foul and no substitute is available, he shall remain in the game.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: A legal screen is set when the screener remains stationary with both feet on the floor before contact occurs. A moving screen, where the screener leans or shifts into the defender, is an illegal screen and an offensive foul.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: Each team is entitled to seven charged timeouts during regulation play. Each timeout lasts 75 seconds. No team may be granted more than four timeouts in the fourth period and no more than two in the last three minutes.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: If the score is tied at the end of the fourth period, play shall resume with an overtime period of five minutes. As many overtime periods as necessary shall be played until a winner is decided.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: The game shall be started with a jump ball in the center circle between any two opponents. The jump ball is tossed by the referee, and jumpers may tap the ball only after it reaches its highest point.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: The shot clock shall be 24 seconds. The offensive team must attempt a field goal that strikes the rim before the shot clock expires. After an offensive rebound the shot clock is reset to 14 seconds rather than 24.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: The ball is out of bounds when it touches a player who is out of bounds, the floor, or any object on or outside a boundary line. The ball is awarded to the opposing team at the nearest spot of the violation.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: On a throw-in, the inbounding player must release the ball within five seconds of receiving it from the official. A five-second inbound violation results in a turnover and the ball awarded to the opponent at the same spot.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: A team in possession in its backcourt must advance the ball across the midcourt line within eight seconds. Failure to advance past midcourt in eight seconds is a violation and the ball is awarded to the opposing team.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: A free throw is the privilege given a player to score one point by an unhindered attempt from the free throw line. The shooter must release the ball within ten seconds and may not cross the line until the ball touches the rim.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: A player shall not dribble a second time after his first dribble has ended, unless he loses control of the ball. Dribbling again after gathering the ball is a double dribble violation, also called an illegal dribble.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: A player shall not intentionally strike the ball with any part of the leg or foot. Kicking the ball intentionally is a kicked ball violation; the shot clock is reset to 14 seconds if fewer than 14 remain.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: An offensive player shall not remain in the free throw lane, known as the key or the paint, for more than three seconds while his team controls the ball. This offensive three-second violation results in a turnover.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: A defensive player shall not remain in the lane for more than three seconds unless he is actively guarding an opponent. The penalty for defensive three seconds is a technical foul free throw and continued possession.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: A player of the team in control in the frontcourt may not cause the ball to go into the backcourt and be the first to touch it. This over-and-back backcourt violation awards the ball to the opposing team.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: A player who receives the ball while progressing or upon completion of a dribble may take two steps in coming to a stop, passing or shooting the ball. Taking more than two steps without dribbling is traveling.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: Goaltending occurs when a player touches the ball during a field goal attempt while the ball is on its downward flight above the rim level. Touching the ball or the basket while the ball is on the rim is basket interference.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: A technical foul is assessed for unsportsmanlike conduct, including disrespectfully addressing an official, taunting an opponent, or delay of game. Two technical fouls result in ejection from the game.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: A flagrant foul is unnecessary contact committed against an opponent. Flagrant one is unnecessary contact; flagrant two is unnecessary and excessive contact and results in immediate ejection.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: A clear path foul occurs when a personal foul is committed on an offensive player with the ball ahead of the defense in transition, denying a clear path to the basket. The penalty is two free throws and possession.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: A player who commits his sixth personal foul shall be disqualified and must leave the game immediately. Six personal fouls is the disqualification limit for an individual player in regulation and overtime combined.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: Instant replay review shall be triggered for made baskets at the end of a period, flagrant foul penalty determination, and out of bounds calls in the last two minutes. Officials review the play at the replay center.

title: NBA Official Playing Rules
text: Each team is entitled to one coach's challenge per game, with a second challenge awarded if the first is successful. A challenge may contest a called foul, an out of bounds violation, or goaltending.

title: Michael Jordan
text: Michael Jordan is an American former professional basketball player who won six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls, earning six Finals MVP awards. Widely regarded as the greatest player of all time, he won five regular season MVP awards and ten scoring titles as a shooting guard.

title: LeBron James
text: LeBron James is an American professional basketball player who became the NBA all-time leading scorer, surpassing Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's career points record in 2023. A four-time champion with the Cavaliers, Heat and Lakers, he is a four-time MVP known for longevity and all-around play as a forward.

title: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar
text: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar is an American former center famous for his unstoppable skyhook shot. He held the NBA all-time scoring record for nearly four decades, won six championships with the Milwaukee Bucks and Los Angeles Lakers, and a record six regular season MVP awards.

title: Stephen Curry
text: Stephen Curry is an American point guard for the Golden State Warriors who revolutionized basketball with his three-point shooting range. The greatest shooter in NBA history, he holds the record for career three-pointers made, won four championships and was the first unanimous MVP.

title: Magic Johnson
text: Magic Johnson is an American former point guard who led the Los Angeles Lakers to five championships during the Showtime era. As a rookie in 1980 he won Finals MVP playing center in the deciding game, and his no-look passing made him one of the greatest playmakers ever.

title: Larry Bird
text: Larry Bird is an American former forward who won three championships with the Boston Celtics and three consecutive regular season MVP awards from 1984 to 1986. Nicknamed the Hick from French Lick, his rivalry with Magic Johnson revived the league in the 1980s.

title: Bill Russell
text: Bill Russell was an American center who won eleven NBA championships with the Boston Celtics, the most titles of any player in league history. A defensive anchor and shot blocker, he won five MVP awards and became the first Black head coach in major American professional sports.

title: Wilt Chamberlain
text: Wilt Chamberlain was an American center who scored 100 points in a single game in 1962, the highest single game total in NBA history. He averaged 50 points per game over an entire season and holds dozens of scoring and rebounding records that still stand.

title: Shaquille O'Neal
text: Shaquille O'Neal is an American former center, one of the most dominant players ever, who won three consecutive championships with the Los Angeles Lakers from 2000 to 2002 alongside Kobe Bryant, earning three straight Finals MVP awards, and a fourth title with the Miami Heat.

title: Tim Duncan
text: Tim Duncan is a former power forward who spent his entire career with the San Antonio Spurs, winning five championships. Nicknamed the Big Fundamental for his understated bank shot and footwork, he is widely considered the greatest power forward in NBA history.

title: Kobe Bryant
text: Kobe Bryant was an American shooting guard who spent twenty seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers, winning five championships. Nicknamed the Black Mamba, he scored 81 points against the Toronto Raptors in 2006, the second highest single game total in NBA history.

title: Hakeem Olajuwon
text: Hakeem Olajuwon is a Nigerian-American former center who led the Houston Rockets to back-to-back championships in 1994 and 1995. His footwork in the post, known as the Dream Shake, made him nearly unguardable, and he remains the NBA all-time leader in blocked shots.

title: Dirk Nowitzki
text: Dirk Nowitzki is a German former power forward who spent 21 seasons with the Dallas Mavericks and led them to the 2011 championship over the Miami Heat. His signature one-legged fadeaway jumper made him the highest scoring European player in NBA history.

title: Giannis Antetokounmpo
text: Giannis Antetokounmpo is a Greek professional forward for the Milwaukee Bucks, nicknamed the Greek Freak for his rare combination of size and speed. A two-time regular season MVP, he led the Bucks to the 2021 championship with a 50-point closeout game in the Finals.

title: Nikola Jokic
text: Nikola Jokic is a Serbian center for the Denver Nuggets, a three-time regular season MVP renowned for his passing and triple-doubles from the center position. Drafted 41st overall, he led Denver to its first championship in 2023 and won Finals MVP.

title: 1998 NBA Finals
text: The 1998 NBA Finals were won by the Chicago Bulls, who defeated the Utah Jazz four games to two for their sixth championship. Michael Jordan hit the series-winning shot over Bryon Russell in Game 6 and was named Finals MVP, completing the Bulls' second three-peat.

title: Showtime (basketball)
text: Showtime was the nickname for the fast-break style of the Los Angeles Lakers during the 1980s, orchestrated by Magic Johnson and coached by Pat Riley. The up-tempo era produced five championships and made the Forum the entertainment capital of basketball.

title: Chicago Bulls
text: The Chicago Bulls are an American professional basketball team that dominated the 1990s, winning six championships in two three-peats behind Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen. Their 72-win season in 1995-96 stood as the league record for two decades.

title: Celtics-Lakers rivalry
text: The Celtics-Lakers rivalry is the most storied in the NBA: the Boston Celtics and Los Angeles Lakers have met in the Finals twelve times, more than any other pair of teams. The rivalry peaked in the 1960s and again in the 1980s with Bird against Magic.

title: Three-point field goal
text: The three-point field goal was adopted by the NBA for the 1979-80 season after originating in the ABA. Initially a novelty attempted a few times per game, the three-pointer became central to modern offenses, with league-wide attempts rising every decade since its introduction.
